notes: **2026-09-06** — (worktree `rf-registry`, branch `fix/bugs-selftest-lock-liveness`, off `master` `0b715128`) — **Lock-liveness self-test pid-reuse fixture flake fixed (CI run 34019219777; `.claude/pipeline/2026-09-06-lock-liveness/reader.md` + `ruling.md`).** The (f) PID-REUSE fixture in `scripts/campaign/bugs.mjs` forged a stale owner's `bootAt` as `Date.now() - LOCK_ABANDON_MS*10` (20 min before "now") instead of relative to the machine's real boot; `BOOT_STAMP_SLOP_MS` only measures the GAP between the forged and real stamps, so a `ubuntu-latest` runner whose actual `os.uptime()` happened to be ~20 minutes when the self-test ran made the impostor's forged boot read as the SAME boot, and the waiter spun its whole `LOCK_SPIN_MS` budget and gave up — the three checks after it inherited the mess purely because the fixtures share `lockDir` state, not from any independent defect. Fix, `bugs.mjs` self-test fixtures only (no lock-primitive change): the forged `bootAt` is now `bootStamp() - 365 * 24 * 3600_000` (one year before the REAL boot, never within 5 s of it on any conceivable uptime); the two checks that used to assert exit-code-then-regex separately are folded into ONE verdict+end-state check (`{code, verdict: /predates this boot/.test(out), ageBased: /age|abandon|last resort/i.test(out)}` against `{0, true, false}`); the pid-reuse block now kills AND awaits the impostor child (`awaitExit`) and clears its own `lockDir` in a `finally`; the owner-write-failure fixture now clears `lockDir` itself before its own precondition check instead of assuming the previous fixture's cleanliness; a give-up print now precedes the write-landed check. Self-test check count: 290 → 289 (the one ruling-approved fold).
